description: Create an Airflow DAG for saas_metrics that monitors data freshness of 12 warehouse tables against per-table thresholds stored in a config table, and alerts on breaches. The DAG runs every 15 minutes and should: (1) read active freshness rules (table, timestamp column, max_lag_minutes, severity, business_hours_only), (2) for each rule compute lag = now_utc - max(timestamp column), using dynamic task mapping, (3) collect breaches, (4) send one consolidated alert per severity, (5) suppress repeat alerts for the same table for 2 hours using a state table, (6) send a recovery notice when a previously breached table becomes fresh.
edge_cases: max(timestamp) on an empty table returns NULL; NULL lag must be treated as a breach, not as fresh
Timestamp columns stored as local time without zone must be converted using the rule's declared timezone before computing lag
business_hours_only rules must be evaluated in the rule's business timezone, including weekends
A check query that fails (table missing, permissions) must be reported as a monitoring failure, separately from a freshness breach
catchup must be False; catching up missed 15-minute runs would send stale alerts
common_failure_modes: FM7: NULL lag compared with a threshold evaluates to NULL/False and an empty table is reported fresh
FM2: Naive local timestamps compared against UTC now produce a constant offset in lag
FM6: No suppression state causes an alert storm every 15 minutes
